decisions.reason: Even though it was no longer visible on the website after 2019, transactional email is highly aligned with the firm's core messaging infrastructure and R&D base, so management would be more likely to retain or fold it into the core platform than withdraw it outright.

Document capture and recognition is adjacent to the firm's workflow business but draws on less directly related knowledge than messaging and security, and its disappearance from the website suggests management would refocus resources on areas with stronger absorptive fit.

Email and fax conversion still supports regulated customers moving between legacy and digital channels, and this is close enough to the firm's established multichannel communications expertise to justify continuation despite lower visibility.

As a narrow fax optimization feature that was no longer promoted, it is the kind of closely related capability the firm can easily absorb into existing services and discontinue as a separate market offer.

Sandbox threat protection fits the firm's secure messaging position very well, and with in-house R&D the firm has strong capacity to learn from use and keep improving it even if it is no longer marketed prominently on its own.

Multi-engine virus scanning is tightly connected to the firm's email security know-how and infrastructure, so management would likely retain it as part of the core secure communications stack rather than remove it.
